chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The Lafayette audience: tougher because they were black
summary: At the all-black Lafayette he did the Loew's State act and says black audiences criticize a black act harder than white audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well the interesting thing is that you were performing also for the Lafayette Theater and the contrast between performing in Harlem and performing downtown. Audiences were completely different.
What were you doing up in the Lafayette Theater?
Doing the old act. The act we did at Loews State, you know.
Were they a tougher audience to deal with or were they an easier audience?

'Cause you're black. And the white audience, the audience is easy because you're colored and they're white. Black audience is tough because they're black and you're black. The criticism was much harder on a negro act than they were on a white act.
Did Nazarro set up the Lafayette Theater gig as well?
Yep. We booked them both, booked them both.
So you must have been making a lot of money at this particular time.
That's only one week, man. How much can you make in one week?
Who else was performing at Lafayette with you?
